What is the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis code for this patient?

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: Caucasian woman with insulin-dependent diabetes and hypertension
Age: 51 years

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient was admitted with a perimesencephalic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) in the prepontine, interpeduncular, ambient, and crural cisterns. She had a previous SAH due to a 6mm aneurysm in the anterior communicating artery (Acomm), which was treated with endovascular coiling.

HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient's hospital course was complicated by vasospasm and cerebral salt wasting. She was treated with hypervolemia, hypertension, intra-arterial nicardipine, and sodium and volume supplementation. After discharge, she returned to work with no residual neurologic deficits.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
N/A

FOLLOW-UP:
The patient had a follow-up magnetic resonance imaging and angiography performed six months later, which demonstrated no vascular abnormalities.

CONDITION AT DISCHARGE:
The patient was discharged home in good condition on post-bleed day 10.

text:
The most likely principal diagnosis code is **I60.8 (Other subarachnoid haemorrhage)**.

The admission was for a perimesencephalic subarachnoid haemorrhage, which is a non-aneurysmal pattern of bleeding centred on the prepontine, interpeduncular, ambient, and crural cisterns. ICD-10-AM has no dedicated code for this presentation, so I60.8 is the closest specific category. The source-specific I60.0–I60.7 codes don't apply, because the current bleed isn't attributed to a named artery. The prior anterior communicating artery aneurysm was a separate, earlier event and doesn't change the principal diagnosis for this admission.

If the coding team can't justify the non-aneurysmal classification, the fallback is **I60.9 (Subarachnoid haemorrhage, unspecified)**. The discharge diagnosis section is blank in this summary, so the final code should be confirmed against the full clinical record and local coding guidelines.
